title: The Early History of the Internet
summary: How Vint Cerf's persistent experimentation with shared rules for sending data in small pieces led to a reliable way to connect separate computer networks, creating the early internet.
poll: The invention of the internet changed how people share information more than almost any other invention in history.

versions.title: The Early History of the Internet
versions.text:
Long ago, machines did not talk to each other. Each group worked alone. This was a big problem.

A man named Vint had a plan. He worked with other men. He wanted machines to talk. He tried new ways.

Vint was not alone. Other men tried too. This was hard. It took a long time.

Vint made a new plan. He made a set of rules. The rules let machines share files. This way was better.

One day, the new way worked. Two groups talked well. This was a big change.

Today, many folks use the web. Machines share files fast. We thank Vint for this plan.

versions.title: The Early History of the Internet
versions.text:
Long before the modern internet existed, no dependable method existed for separate computer networks to communicate adequately with one another, and this constituted a constant, frustrating predicament for scientists and researchers throughout nearly the entirety of early computing history. Each separate network functioned completely alone and independently, at considerable inconvenience.

A man named Vint Cerf possessed a bold and genuinely ambitious vision entirely of his own, so he labored diligently alongside other brilliant researchers within a busy, bustling laboratory and dreamed, quite persistently and stubbornly, of someday interconnecting separate networks mechanically. He devoted many long, arduous years meticulously testing countless experimental technical approaches to accomplish this difficult, elusive objective that had eluded so many previous researchers before him across generations upon generations.

Vint was certainly not the sole inventor attempting this ambitious, seemingly impossible feat at that particular juncture in history, since other skilled experimenters across several different nations also labored tirelessly and persistently to engineer a dependable method for interconnecting networks, frequently toiling for years without ever achieving much lasting, dependable success whatsoever. This slow, maddeningly uncertain method remained quite difficult and frustrating, and it consumed a remarkably long duration to construct even a single, properly functioning link.

Vint and a growing circle of fellow experimenters finally and decisively resolved to attempt something entirely novel and quite different altogether from anything previously attempted by earlier generations. He helped formulate a set of protocols that allowed data to traverse small, meticulously organized packets between networks. These protocols allowed computers to locate each other and exchange data steadily, quietly, and reliably, functioning continuously without requiring constant supervision. This new, meticulously engineered method turned out to be remarkably and surprisingly more efficient and effective than almost anyone had honestly anticipated at that particular juncture in history.

One famous and truly historic day, Vint's innovative new method finally functioned extremely well indeed. Two separate networks finally interconnected completely and exchanged data rapidly, without requiring any manual intervention whatsoever. This remarkable breakthrough quickly became a massive and truly lasting transformation for the entire modern world, affecting nearly every corner of daily existence everywhere, from household devices to enormous global corporations and institutions.

Today, countless people all around the entire globe use the internet every single day, frequently connected through smart devices too. Many people exchange data effortlessly, every single time, without even pausing for a brief second thought about the remarkable mechanism behind how it actually functions. We can gratefully thank Vint for devising this remarkably clever and genuinely lasting innovation that transformed modern human communication forever and irrevocably.
